records.body: There comes a point in life when one discovers that one's skin has apparently resigned from its previous occupation and taken up a new career as parchment. This is where CeraVe Moisturizing Cream enters the story. I had seen the enormous tubs of the stuff before and assumed, from the packaging, that it was probably intended either for dermatology patients or for waterproofing garden furniture. Then I tried it. And, irritatingly, it is excellent. It is thick without being unpleasantly greasy, absorbs well, and does exactly what one wants a moisturiser to do: it makes dry skin feel considerably less like something archaeologists ought to be carbon-dating. The formula contains ceramides and hyaluronic acid, which sounds reassuringly scientific and allows one to apply it with the quiet confidence of someone participating in advanced dermatological research rather than merely smearing cream on one's elbows. And it works. Hands? Better. Arms? Better. Face? Better. General winter-induced transformation into Tutankhamun? Arrested. The tub is also commendably large, which means one can use a sensible amount rather than treating every application as though one were spreading the last teaspoon of wartime butter. There is, however, one important qualification. The price. At the right sale price, this is unquestionably a five-star product. At full price, I begin examining the label more closely to determine whether the ceramides were individually harvested by monks in Switzerland. CeraVe pricing seems to exist in two states: SALE: "Good heavens, that's excellent value. I'll have one." NOT SALE: "For moisturiser?" So I do what any rational consumer does. I wait. Amazon knocks several dollars off it, I pounce, and another large tub arrives to continue the apparently endless task of preventing bits of me from becoming dessicated. The product itself deserves five stars. The pricing occasionally deserves a sternly raised eyebrow. ⭐⭐⭐⭐⭐ when on sale. ⭐⭐⭐⭐ if you've paid full whack and are now pretending not to mind. Mister Twiggly P.S. As demonstrated in the photograph, the lid is capable of supporting one moderately substantial bear. This is not one of the advertised dermatological benefits. P.P.S. I have not personally tested the moisturising properties. My complexion is naturally magnificent.

records.body: I got the CeraVe Moisturizing Cream because I’ve been trying to make skincare a real part of my daily routine since starting HRT. Moisturizing feels like a small habit that helps me feel more comfortable and connected to my body, and I like that this cream works for both my face and body so I can keep things simple. The texture feels rich without being greasy, absorbs well, and leaves my skin feeling softer and more hydrated. I also appreciate the ceramides and hyaluronic acid because it feels like I’m supporting my skin barrier instead of just putting on lotion. The fragrance-free formula works well for me because it stays discreet without adding an obvious scent, and the 19 oz size makes it easier to stay consistent. Overall, this has become a gentle, practical moisturizer that fits the healthier, softer skincare routine I’m trying to build.
